issues.body:
The header comment added by this PR claims the LWS workflow is held to the "same multi-arch and pre-push assurance contract so either server image regressing to a single architecture or an unscanned push fails this gate."

The multi-arch half is genuinely enforced. The pre-push half is not. `assert_lws_container_contract` retrieves the smoke build, the smoke run, the Trivy scan and the push with `_, smoke = _step_named(...)`, `_, trivy = ...`, `_, push = ...` — every index is discarded, and no ordering comparison is made between them. Only the QEMU/Buildx pair is index-checked.

Consequence: reorder `lws-container.yml` so `Publish amd64 + arm64 image index` sits before `Scan native image (fail on fixable HIGH or CRITICAL)` — i.e. publish the multi-arch image to ghcr.io and only then scan it — and this contract still passes green. That is precisely the "unscanned push" regression the comment says is caught. The ordering IS the security property here; asserting only that a Trivy step exists somewhere in the job with `exit-code: "1"` does not establish that anything was scanned before publication.

The same gap exists in the pre-existing `assert_release_container_contract`, so this PR replicates it rather than introducing it — but the PR is what adds the explicit claim that the gate covers it, which makes the claim untraceable to the code.
issues.fix_hint:
Keep the indices and assert the pipeline order, e.g.:

    smoke_index, smoke = _step_named(steps, "Build native amd64 image for smoke and scan")
    smoke_run_index, smoke_run = _step_named(steps, "Smoke native image (health, fail-closed mutation, non-root)")
    trivy_index, trivy = _step_named(steps, "Scan native image (fail on fixable HIGH or CRITICAL)")
    push_index, push = _step_named(steps, "Publish amd64 + arm64 image index")
    assert smoke_index < smoke_run_index < trivy_index < push_index, (
        "the native artifact must be smoked and scanned BEFORE any registry push"
    )

Then add a mutation test proving that assertion is non-vacuous — e.g. reorder the scan step after the push step in the fixture text and assert `assert_lws_container_contract` raises. Apply the same to `assert_release_container_contract` if you want the comment's "both servers" claim to hold, or narrow the comment to what is actually asserted.
issues.title: LWS contract never asserts smoke/Trivy precede the push, yet the added comment claims an unscanned push fails the gate

issues.body:
`assert buildx_indices[0] < qemu_index, "native gate must run before QEMU is enabled"` checks only where `docker/setup-buildx-action` appears relative to `docker/setup-qemu-action`. It says nothing about the native gate (the build/smoke/scan steps) — those could all sit after QEMU and this passes. A reader trusting the message would believe more is enforced than is.

Separately, this pins Buildx-before-QEMU for `lws-container.yml`, while `assert_release_container_contract` pins the exact opposite (`qemu_index < buildx_indices[0]`, "QEMU must be registered before Buildx") for `release.yml`. Docker's own documented order is setup-qemu then setup-buildx, because the docker-container-driver builder enumerates its supported platforms when buildkitd starts; a builder booted before binfmt registration may not advertise linux/arm64. I have not been able to confirm whether the arm64 build actually fails in practice (binfmt_misc registrations are host-global and `--install -F` preloads the interpreter, which often makes this forgiving), and `lws-container.yml` is tag-triggered so it may not have run. Flagging as a risk, not a confirmed break — but this PR converts the ordering into a required contract, so aligning LWS with release.yml later would now go red.
issues.fix_hint: Either reword the message to what is checked ("Buildx must be set up before QEMU") or assert the property the message describes, e.g. `assert trivy_index < qemu_index, "the native gate must complete before emulation is enabled"`. Independently, confirm the arm64 leg of `lws-container.yml` actually builds under Buildx-before-QEMU (a workflow_dispatch run is enough); if it does not, fix the workflow order to match release.yml and flip the assertion rather than pinning the current order.
issues.title: Assertion message does not match what is checked, and pins an ordering opposite to the sibling release.yml contract

issues.body:
`assert permissions.get("id-token") == "write"` and `assert permissions.get("attestations") == "write"` require those grants on the `publish` job. But `lws-container.yml` contains no `actions/attest-build-provenance` step, no cosign step, and nothing else that consumes an OIDC token — grep for `attest|cosign|id-token` returns only the two permission lines themselves. The BuildKit attestations it does produce (`provenance: mode=max`, `sbom: true`) are attached to the image in the registry and need only `packages: write`.

So the test now pins two unused elevated permissions as contract: a least-privilege cleanup that drops them would fail this gate for no security reason, and the assertion reads as if attestation coverage is being verified when it is not.
issues.fix_hint: Either drop the `id-token` / `attestations` assertions and keep only `packages: write` (which the push genuinely needs), or — if signed provenance is the intent for this image — add the `actions/attest-build-provenance` step to `lws-container.yml` and assert THAT step exists, so the permissions are justified by a consumer the test also pins.
issues.title: Test makes unused id-token/attestations permissions a required contract

issues.body:
The contract asserts the smoke step's `run:` line verbatim but not its `env:`. `crates/sparq-lws-core/tests/container-smoke.sh` branches on `if [ "${LWS_CONTAINER_SKIP_BUILD:-0}" != "1" ]` and, when unset, runs its own `docker build --tag "${IMAGE}"`.

That means dropping `LWS_CONTAINER_SKIP_BUILD: "1"` from the workflow makes the smoke step rebuild and overwrite `sparq-lws-core:smoke` with a plain `docker build` artifact. The smoke would then be validating a different image than the buildx-produced one, and the subsequent Trivy scan of `sparq-lws-core:smoke` would scan that replacement rather than the gated artifact. This contract passes green through that regression.
issues.fix_hint:
Assert the env alongside the run line:

    assert smoke_run.get("env", {}).get("LWS_CONTAINER_SKIP_BUILD") == "1", (
        "the smoke must reuse the buildx-gated image, not rebuild its own"
    )
issues.title: Smoke step's LWS_CONTAINER_SKIP_BUILD env is not pinned, so the scanned image and the smoked image can silently diverge

issues.body:
The replaced comment documented why the step exists, citing sq-w1dxx, sq-fvzi6, sq-n6rv and sq-p9xq, and explained the concrete failure mode: a `workflow_dispatch` dev-build must never push `:latest` because `deploy/paas` and `deploy/aws` pin that tag.

The replacement collapses this to "a workflow_dispatch dev build must never push a deployment-followed tag" and drops all four bead IDs and the `[OPUS-5]` attribution while retaining `[GPT-5]`. Those assertions are still live in the file (`test_live_dispatch_tags_never_collide_with_canonical_tags`, `test_unnamespaced_dispatch_tag_fails_contract`, `test_ungated_latest_tag_fails_contract`, `test_dropping_the_setup_dependency_fails_contract`), so the CI-side comment now under-describes and mis-attributes work it still gates. Per the repo's traceability conventions, bead IDs on a gate comment are the link back to why the gate exists.

No functional impact — the `run:` line is unchanged and the step still executes the same file.
issues.fix_hint: Extend rather than replace: keep the existing `[OPUS-5] sq-w1dxx` paragraph (and the sq-fvzi6 / sq-n6rv / sq-p9xq references) and append a new `[GPT-5] sq-fqrv4` sentence covering the added sparq-lws-core contract. The renamed step title ("Release container contracts ...") is a good change — keep it.
issues.title: Comment rewrite drops the sq-w1dxx dispatch-tag rationale and bead IDs the test still enforces

verdict.summary:
The new LWS contract assertions are real and non-vacuous: I traced every assertion in assert_lws_container_contract against the live .github/workflows/lws-container.yml (job `publish`, 9 steps) and they all hold — permissions, 40-hex-pinned setup-qemu-action, images=ghcr.io/sparq-org/sparq-lws-core, the Dockerfile path, load/push flags, tags=sparq-lws-core:smoke, the container-smoke.sh run line (script and Dockerfile both exist on disk), Trivy exit-code "1", and the amd64+arm64 push with provenance=mode=max + sbom. The added mutation test is genuinely non-vacuous: the needle "platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64" matches only the push step (the smoke step's "platforms: linux/amd64" is not a prefix match for the longer needle), so the count=1 replace hits the right line and the platforms set assertion goes red. (I could not execute the suite — PyYAML is absent and no pip is available — so this is source-traced, not executed.)

The blocking gap is an overclaim. The comment this PR adds to the test header states the LWS workflow is kept under the "same pre-push assurance contract so ... an unscanned push fails this gate", but assert_lws_container_contract discards every step index except QEMU/Buildx (`_, smoke`, `_, trivy`, `_, push`) and never compares them. Moving `Publish amd64 + arm64 image index` above the Trivy scan — the exact regression the comment says is caught — still passes. Relatedly, the assertion labelled "native gate must run before QEMU is enabled" only checks the Buildx *setup* index, not the native build/smoke/scan steps, and it pins the opposite ordering to the sibling release.yml contract.

Secondary: the test now makes unused id-token/attestations grants a required contract, and pins the smoke `run:` line without the LWS_CONTAINER_SKIP_BUILD env that keeps the smoked image identical to the scanned one. The docs-quality.yml comment rewrite also drops the sq-w1dxx dispatch-tag rationale that the file still enforces.
